messages.author: 9be5ae75921aca4a
messages.subject: Variational HMM
parts:
Hi all,

I am trying to get the component means as from a HMM gauss mixture model. Now I am aware of the complications caused by the label switching problem. But I expected the VB model to converge to one mode of the log posterior and atleast model thoee params. But this isn't the case. I have included the test function (in R) and the mode (stanfile).

As can be seen the true model and the estimated do not line up at all.

Am I doing something wrong here? Is the label fitting problem affecting the answer?

Any comments/ remarks would appreciated.

Thanks,
Sachin

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Variational HMM
parts:
Can you fit it with MCMC?

With K=3 there's a chance you can recover the parameters
if the mu[k]/sigma[k] are well separated. You will have
a label switching problem, but presumably that's not the
problem for ADVI.

- Bob

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Variational HMM
parts:
On Saturday, April 16, 2016 at 7:09:35 PM UTC-4, Sachinthaka Abeywardana wrote:
So I tried normal stan (MCMC) and it worked perfectly. But now I'm getting this new warning I didn't see before: 
"There were 1469 divergent transitions after warmup. Increasing adapt_delta above 0.8 may help. "

How do I play around with this adapt_delta parameter?

Include

control = list(adapt_delta = 0.95)

in the call to stan(). It may need to go higher than 0.95 though.

Ben

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Variational HMM
parts:
On Sunday, April 17, 2016 at 12:39:17 AM UTC-4, Sachinthaka Abeywardana wrote:
Just letting you know that I had that warning when calling the R function vb(). However, R complains that vb does not have a 'control' parameter.

However, when i ran this again I DID NOT get the warning about divergent transitions.

I think you accidentally called stan() or sampling() when you got that warning. The concept of a divergent transition is only relevant for HMC, so conversely vb() doesn't have a control list.

Ben

see http://arxiv.org/abs/1603.00788 where we study this for a stochastic volatility model.

messages.author: 49e107cb0f8a3d27
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Variational HMM
parts:
This is an interesting comment. But to clarify, are you saying implemented a coordinate ascent mean-field variational inference, or an ADVI implementation in Python? And are you saying this implementation gave an accurate answer for the approximate posterior means, that it converged quickly, or both? Mean-field will in general not do well at capturing approximate posterior means for non-iid data. But if you got that to work, that’s pretty cool.

Dustin
